title: Stay With What You Wanted to Say
learningGoals: Identify the meaning you wanted to share
Preserve the point with flexible wording

deeperExplanation.question: What if the exact word matters?
deeperExplanation.answer: Names, technical terms and particular requests sometimes need precise wording. You can take time, clarify the term or use another channel alongside speaking. Preserving meaning includes preserving a necessary word when you choose to. It does not require forcing the sound with increasing pressure. A short explanation such as this is the name I mean can keep the purpose available while you find a usable way to communicate it.

sections.narration:
Welcome. Today we are exploring Stay With What You Wanted to Say. You begin explaining a preference, then a word feels difficult. You replace the point with something easier and leave the conversation thinking: that was not really what I wanted to say.

In this session, we will identify the meaning you wanted to share, separate wording from intention, and preserve the point with flexible wording. I will explain the idea, show a visual example, and invite you to try it in a small experience of your own. You can ask me a question or switch to reading at any point. We will finish by choosing what, if anything, you want to take into a real conversation.

sections.narration:
You begin explaining a preference, then a word feels difficult. You replace the point with something easier and leave the conversation thinking: that was not really what I wanted to say.

Sometimes a synonym genuinely improves clarity. Sometimes it is a hurried escape that changes the message. Notice the difference through your intention. Ask whether the listener received what mattered. You can choose a shorter or different sentence and still stay with the message.

A short explanation such as this is the name I mean can keep the purpose available while you find a usable way to communicate it.

Changed, unchanged or uncertain experiences are all information.

sections.narration: Staying with meaning does not mean forcing through pain or refusing to stop. A pause, another time or another communication channel may serve the meaning. The decision belongs to you. A changed, unchanged or uncertain experience is information, not a grade. You do not have to report relief for this attempt to count as exploration.

sections.narration: Choose one ordinary point you want to express. After the exchange, note whether the intended meaning was shared. During focused practice, you can deliberately explore this one tool. In an everyday conversation, give most of your attention to the message and the other person. A familiar support can be available if it helps; you do not have to monitor the tool throughout the exchange.
